sn52.3:1.1: The Sutanu (“slender”) river is mentioned only here. Anuruddha is often depicted in these out-of-the-way settings.
sn52.3:2.8: The exact sense of “lower”, “middle”, and “higher” dhammas here is unclear.  Given the context of Anuruddha’s psychic powers, I follow Bodhi’s suggestion that we interpret in line with AN 3.76, understanding dhamma as the “principle” governing the relationship between mental quality and states of rebirth (SN 12.20:2.3). The commentary, alternatively, cites the Abhidhamma Dhammasaṅgaṇī (Ds 1.1:40.1), which has the three as one of its triads in the sense of good, mundane wholesome, and transcendent mental phenomena. This analysis, however, does not really reflect Sutta usage, which typically speaks of simply lower and higher dhammas (SN 46.2:10.2). Moreover, we would expect a plural in that case.
